# Machine Learning in Quantitative Finance

## Applying Statistical Learning to Financial Market Data

**Ebube Anozie**  
PhD Student in Applied Mathematics  
University of Colorado Boulder

[View the code on GitHub](https://github.com/ebubeanozie/quant-ML-project)

---

## About the Project

This portfolio explores the application of machine learning
methods to quantitative-finance problems.

Throughout the semester, I will apply statistical learning
techniques to financial market data, investigate their
computational properties, evaluate model performance, and
interpret the results from a quantitative-finance perspective.

The project is developed as part of **CSCI 5612: Machine
Learning for Data Science** at the University of Colorado
Boulder.

---

## Research Question

> **Can machine-learning methods identify useful and robust
> patterns in financial market data?**

The project investigates this question through a sequence of
supervised and unsupervised learning methods.

## Methods

The project will progressively incorporate the machine-learning
methods covered in CSCI 5612.

| Method | Objective | Status |
|:---|:---|:---:|
| Data Preparation | Clean and transform financial data | In progress |
| Regression | Model relationships between financial variables | Upcoming |
| Clustering | Identify groups and patterns in financial data | Upcoming |
| Dimensionality Reduction | Extract important latent structure | Upcoming |
| Ensemble Methods | Improve predictive performance | Upcoming |

---

## Why Quantitative Finance?

Financial markets generate large, noisy, and high-dimensional
datasets. Machine learning provides a collection of tools for
extracting structure from these datasets and developing
data-driven models.

My broader interest lies at the intersection of:

**Applied Mathematics · Machine Learning · Numerical Methods · Quantitative Finance**

This project is an opportunity to explore how these areas can
work together.

---

## About Me

I am a PhD student in Applied Mathematics at the University of
Colorado Boulder.

My interests include quantitative finance, machine learning,
mathematical modeling, numerical methods, and computational
science.

I am particularly interested in developing mathematical and
computational methods for large-scale, data-driven problems.
